headline: A dry, chilly Tuesday gives way to a high-impact Thanksgiving storm: rain reaches Kentucky Wednesday evening while a strengthening Upstate wedge brings heavy rain and strong northeast wind; Kentucky then turns windy with wet snow late Thanksgiving
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: Sunny, chilly weather holds today before clouds increase tonight. Rain reaches Central Kentucky mainly Wednesday evening and becomes widespread overnight. Periods of rain and strong wind continue Thanksgiving as a compact upper low pivots across the state; colder wraparound precipitation should mix with or change to wet snow Thursday evening and night, with minor grassy or elevated-surface slush possible before the early-Friday endpoint.
kentucky.currentConditions: At 6:55 AM EST, KDVK reported 28°F with a 27°F dew point, clear sky, light northeast wind and 10-mile visibility. At 7:54 AM, KLEX reported 29°F with a 25°F dew point, northeast wind near 9 mph and clear sky. College of DuPage radar showed no precipitation over Central Kentucky. No official NWS point alert was active for Danville at the final check.

days.label: Tuesday / Tuesday night
days.hazard: OFFICIAL NWS ALERT STATUS: no active point alert covers Danville at issuance. The independent concern is another localized freeze tonight, especially in sheltered rural valleys. Rain, thunder and hazardous wind are not expected.
days.forecast: Sunny, dry and seasonably cold beneath high pressure. Northeast wind runs 6–12 mph with gusts around 20–25 mph. The most-likely Danville high is near 47°F. Clouds increase late tonight, but precipitation remains absent; after applying the maintained Danville cold correction, the most-likely early-Wednesday low is near 32°F.

days.label: Wednesday / Wednesday night
days.precipitation: Around 20% through early afternoon; 70–80% by evening; 95–100% Wednesday night
days.hazard: OFFICIAL NWS ALERT STATUS: no active point alert covers Danville at issuance. Independent concerns are widespread rain, wet holiday-travel roads, reduced visibility and increasingly gusty wind Wednesday evening and night. Flooding and thunder are not the primary signals.
days.forecast: Clouds thicken through the day. Rain most likely reaches Danville between about 4–8 PM EST, then becomes widespread Wednesday night as the upper disturbances phase. The most-likely high is near 51°F and the most-likely overnight low is near 41°F. East to northeast wind around 5–10 mph becomes gustier after dark, with gusts of 20–30 mph. Roughly 0.50–0.75 inch of rain is possible by daybreak Thanksgiving.

days.label: Thanksgiving / early Friday
days.precipitation: 100% through Thanksgiving; rain and wet snow remain likely Thursday night into the early-Friday endpoint
days.hazard: OFFICIAL NWS ALERT STATUS: no active point alert covers Danville at issuance. Independent concerns are soaking rain, 30–40 mph gusts, poor travel visibility and a late change to wet snow. A trace to one-half inch of grassy or elevated-surface slush is most likely near Danville; isolated amounts near one inch are possible, while widespread road accumulation is not the leading outcome.
days.forecast: Periods of rain continue through much of Thanksgiving as the upper low pivots across Kentucky. Colder wraparound precipitation should mix with or change to wet snow, most likely after about 8 PM, although earlier flakes remain possible. The most-likely high is near 47°F and the most-likely early-Friday low near 31°F. West to northwest wind strengthens to 15–25 mph with gusts around 30–40 mph. Storm-total rainfall from Wednesday night through Friday is expected to reach about 1.25–2.00 inches.

kentucky.bottomLine: Central Kentucky stays dry and chilly today. Rain most likely begins around 4–8 PM Wednesday, becomes widespread Wednesday night and continues through Thanksgiving. Gusts reach 30–40 mph late Thursday, and rain should mix with or change to wet snow Thursday evening or night. Most-likely Danville high/low pairs are 47/32°F, 51/41°F and 47/31°F.
kentucky.confidence: High in today's dry cold; medium-high in Wednesday rain with medium confidence in onset; high in Thanksgiving rain and wind but medium in the wet-snow changeover and accumulation

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson primary · Central/Pickens County comparison
upstate.summary: Mostly cloudy, dry and breezy weather continues today as a classic cold-air-damming wedge strengthens. Rain spreads into the Clemson–Central corridor Wednesday late morning or early afternoon, then becomes steady and locally heavy with strong northeast wind Wednesday afternoon and night. Rain and gusty wind continue Thanksgiving morning before tapering during the afternoon as the coastal low pulls away.
upstate.currentConditions: Around 6:55 AM EST, KCEU reported 55°F with a 43°F dew point, northeast wind near 9 mph and broken cloud layers. KLQK reported about 54°F with an east-northeast breeze and an overcast near 4,200 feet; KGSP also showed northeast wind and extensive cloud cover. College of DuPage radar showed no meaningful precipitation over the Upstate. No official NWS point alert was active for Clemson or Central at the final check. Tempest data was not used.

days.label: Tuesday / Tuesday night
days.hazard: OFFICIAL NWS ALERT STATUS: no active point alert covers Clemson or Central at issuance. The independent concern is a breezy northeast wind as the wedge strengthens. Widespread advisory-level wind, rain, thunder and fog are not expected today.
days.forecast: Mostly cloudy and dry, with the most-likely corridor high near 58°F. East-northeast wind runs 8–14 mph with gusts around 22–30 mph. Clouds thicken tonight as cold-air damming strengthens; the most-likely regional low is near 36°F after applying the maintained KCEU and KLQK corrections. Tempest data was not used.

days.label: Wednesday / Wednesday night
days.precipitation: 60–70% by late morning; 90–100% Wednesday afternoon and night
days.hazard: OFFICIAL NWS ALERT STATUS: no active point alert covers Clemson or Central at issuance. Independent concerns are locally heavy rain, poor visibility, ponding, 35–45 mph gusts and isolated power interruptions. An isolated gust near 50 mph is possible; severe thunderstorms are not the primary concern.
days.forecast: Rain develops approximately 10 AM–2 PM and becomes steady and locally heavy during the late afternoon and night as a strong easterly low-level jet overruns the cool wedge. The most-likely high is near 49°F and the most-likely overnight low near 46°F. Northeast wind increases to 15–25 mph with gusts around 35–45 mph. The stable wedge should suppress severe convection, but embedded heavier rain bands and low visibility may affect holiday travel.

days.label: Thanksgiving / early Friday
days.precipitation: 95% during the morning, falling below 20% late afternoon and evening
days.hazard: OFFICIAL NWS ALERT STATUS: no active point alert covers Clemson or Central at issuance. Independent concerns are locally heavy morning rain, poor visibility, ponding and north to northwest gusts of 25–40 mph. No snow or ice is expected in the Clemson–Central corridor.
days.forecast: Rain, locally heavy at times, continues through Thanksgiving morning before tapering approximately 2–6 PM as the coastal low pulls away. The most-likely high is near 55°F, though a brief approach toward 60°F is possible if the wedge erodes faster. North to northwest wind around 8–15 mph may gust 25–40 mph early. The most-likely early-Friday low is near 35°F. Storm-total rainfall should average 1.0–2.0 inches, with localized 2–3+ inch totals possible beneath a persistent band.

upstate.bottomLine: The Upstate remains mostly cloudy and dry today. Rain develops around 10 AM–2 PM Wednesday and becomes heavy at times with 35–45 mph gusts. Thanksgiving begins rainy and windy before improving during the afternoon. Most-likely corridor high/low pairs are 58/36°F, 49/46°F and 55/35°F.
upstate.confidence: High in today's dry wedge development; high in Wednesday rain with medium confidence in amounts and peak gusts; medium in Thanksgiving temperatures and the exact afternoon exit time

sourceNotes: Chris Bailey's November 24 Kentucky Weather Center post and supporting graphics were accepted as authoritative source material for Kentucky. Bailey supports a west-to-east wet-snow swath, slushy accumulation, 30–40 mph gusts and Friday-morning wind chills near 20°F.
Official NWS alerts are kept separate from the independent forecast. No active point alert covered Danville, Clemson or Central at the final check.

NWS Louisville supports 1–2 inches of beneficial rain, 30–35 mph gusts and a late-Thanksgiving/Friday rain-snow transition, but considers meaningful accumulation unlikely because of warm ground and marginal surface temperatures.
NWS Greenville-Spartanburg supports a strong classic cold-air-damming event, an anomalous 60–70-knot easterly low-level jet, heavy rain and impactful wind Wednesday into Thanksgiving morning.

Fresh deterministic COD guidance gives roughly 0.87–1.75 inches of 72-hour precipitation near Danville and 0.44–1.61 inches near Clemson; ensemble guidance supports the selected event-total ranges while retaining higher local Upstate outcomes.
Fresh GEFS, ECENS, GEPS, AIGEFS and AIFS ensembles were used for precipitation, wind, temperature and Kentucky wet-snow probability. Model disagreement in snow accumulation is explicitly retained.
Fresh local GFS3, RRFS, HRRR and RAP BUFKIT profiles for KLEX/KSME/KGSP/KAND were used. Local NAM/NAM-3km/SREF/HiResW files dated November 4 were stale and excluded; RRFS is the current replacement.
The fresh raw-GRIB attempt did not complete validation, so no unvalidated raw-GRIB fields or precipitation totals were used.
COD radar showed both forecast regions precipitation-free at issuance, while GOES-19 imagery showed the expanding Southeast cloud shield without local deep convection.
The WPC Slight Risk is focused on the coastal Carolinas and is not an official point alert for Clemson or Central.
The current accuracy summary, station corrections, empirical temperature widths, fog/timing lessons and model-regime decisions were applied.
Tempest data was excluded from all Upstate analysis and verification.
Daily lows are following-night lows. The third cards extend through the exact early-Friday 72-hour endpoint.
